title: Milvus + WP — E2E Write / Append
description: Proxy → Streaming Client → SN WAL → WP Client → WP services / disk. Ordered operational steps; see E2E-DASHBOARDS.md for metric scope and coverage.

panels.title: E2E Write / Append — read from top to bottom

options.content:
**Proxy → Streaming Client → SN WAL → WP Client → WP services / disk**

Select a time window containing the workload. Channel filters apply to Milvus channel metrics; log filters apply to WP metrics. They are independent identities: use wpcli metadata to map them; there is no automatic channel-to-log or collection-to-log join. Legends identify the actual process.

**No data ≠ healthy zero.** Lazy/error/remote-only metrics may be absent; `./stack.sh verify` records each stage's coverage. Timers overlap and quantiles are not additive. Read each step's guidance before interpreting an idle signal.

panels.title: 1. Proxy — admission, preparation and request completion

options.content: Start here for slow/failed inserts. Compare successful mutation latency with completed request status and queue depth. If writes fail with rate=0, inspect QuotaCenter reduction and memory first: the SN-hosted delegator can trigger query-node memory protection. If the queue grows while downstream latency stays stable, inspect Proxy resources and admission. If produce latency rises too, continue to stage 2. REST/network/client time is outside this successful-mutation timer.

panels.title: Write request completions by status
panels.description: Use status=total for total completions; success/fail/retry are classifications, not additional requests to add to total. In the reference image, streaming rate-limit rejections were reported as retry even with client write retries disabled.

panels.title: Successful mutation latency
panels.description: P50/P95/P99 of observed operations; no observations produce no data/NaN. Check the stage's observation rate. Quantiles from different stages cannot be added or subtracted. Values above the largest finite histogram bucket cannot be resolved accurately.

panels.title: Quota write-rate reduction (0=none, 1=fully reduced)
panels.description: The reference QuotaCenter exports 1 minus the allowed-rate factor. A rising value means MORE restriction. Correlate memory, lag and QuotaCenter logs; this gauge does not name the limiting reason.

panels.title: Process RSS / container memory limit
panels.description: Context for memory protection, including the query/delegator hosted on SN. RSS is not the exact QuotaCenter hardware-metric input; confirm the reason and configured low/high watermarks in QuotaCenter logs/configuration.

panels.title: Inserted rows / second
panels.description: Successful rows/second. Compare mutation latency with request completion rates; internal WAL message counts include control traffic.

panels.title: 2. Proxy Streaming Client — route and send to StreamingNode

options.content: Compare produce latency/status by channel. Unavailable producers suggest routing, ownership or reconnect problems. When producers are available but produce latency grows, compare quota admission delay before inspecting SN in-flight work and WAL append in stage 3. Admission waits can dominate a write while backend append is relatively fast.

panels.description: P50/P95/P99 of observed operations; no observations produce no data/NaN. Check the stage's observation rate. Quantiles from different stages cannot be added or subtracted. Values above the largest finite histogram bucket cannot be resolved accurately.

panels.title: Proxy received payload bytes / second
panels.description: Milvus-recorded input payload, not necessarily acknowledged writes, and not the same byte definition as raw float32 vectors or replicated WAL traffic.

panels.title: Quota delay observations / second
panels.description: Lazy/version-specific. A long admission delay can dominate client latency even while the WAL backend remains comparatively fast.

panels.title: 3. StreamingNode WAL — interceptors and backend append

options.content: Compare full WAL append, backend append and each interceptor. Overlapping timer scopes are not an additive latency breakdown. Inspect retries and per-channel confirmation progress. Backend latency rising points to stage 4; growing interceptor time points to the named interceptor.

panels.title: 4. WP Client inside Milvus — pending appends and replica results

options.content: The WP client runs inside SN; it is not a separate Pod. Compare pending appends and writer outcomes with per-log append latency. Replica counters are attempts, not acknowledged Milvus rows. For failing/slow replicas continue to stage 5; use wp meta log list and wp node list to resolve identities.

panels.title: 5. WP services — append, buffer wait and local disk flush

options.content: Compare individual nodes rather than only a cluster-wide quantile. High buffer wait plus flush time suggests local disk/sync pressure. Check scheduler queues and node resources before changing concurrency. wp ops, wp node log-health and component logs provide the next evidence.

panels.title: 6. Admission and resource pressure — explain sustained slowdown

options.content: Disk admission state is 0=normal, 1=warn, 2=blocked. Compare actual disk use with exported watermarks in the WP reference dashboard. Check the Flush/Checkpoint dashboard for Milvus buffer pressure; WP object-store compaction is a separate background path, not every append's synchronous storage step.

panels.title: Allocated minus confirmed TimeTick
panels.description: Unix-second timestamp difference for the same Pod/channel, not a per-request latency or entry count.
